name: comp-464
title: Pagination Page Select
description: A compact pager of first, previous, next and last arrows wrapped around a centred dropdown listing every page, ticking the current one.
use: Lists with a handful of pages where people want to jump straight to a page number.
avoid: With very many pages: the menu lists every page, so it grows long instead of paging.
a11y: The page select has an aria-label and each arrow is named; menu transitions have no reduced-motion handling. (keyboard: yes, labels: good, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: Five controls sit in a flat row on black: a first-page and a back chevron, an outlined Page 2 selector with a down arrow, then next and last chevrons. The selector opens a tall dark menu of Page 1 through Page 8 with a tick.
behaves: Clicking the selector drops a list of every page; hovering a row fills it grey and picking one updates the trigger label, here from Page 2 to Page 6. The arrows stay still.
customise: currentPage and totalPages set the default selection and menu length; the four arrow icons and selector styling are fixed in the file.
weight: light: One small select and four arrow links; nothing runs in the background.
demo: Page 2 selected out of eight, with menu rows Page 1 to Page 8.
issues: The page select only sets its default value, so it will not follow currentPage when the arrows change it.
polishWhy: Tidy centred selector between arrows; a practical but plain pager.
